selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What main question is being discussed in this passage?
questions.answer: It asks why so much effort is still being made for the Risale-i Nur when even a small part of it can answer very stubborn unbelief.

questions.question: What does the first speaker find surprising?
questions.answer: He finds it surprising that the work for faith keeps growing even though the book already has very strong proofs.

questions.question: What is one reason the questioner thinks extra effort may seem unnecessary?
questions.answer: He thinks even a very small part of the work is already enough to answer strong disbelief.

questions.question: Besides one person’s heart, what larger things need healing?
questions.answer: The shared spiritual condition of people, their common thinking, and the wider moral awareness of society need healing.

questions.question: Why is the image of giant stones important in the passage?
questions.answer: It shows that what is being protected is massive, weighty, and not easy to rebuild.

questions.question: What is the difference between an individual conscience and a general conscience in the passage?
questions.answer: One belongs to a single person, while the other refers to the shared moral and spiritual awareness of many people.

questions.question: What kind of help does the passage say the Qur’an provides?
questions.answer: It provides healing and strong guidance for faith.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the needed proofs?
questions.answer: It describes them as being very firm and powerful, like mountains.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the journey of belief?
questions.answer: It says belief has endless درجات or levels to move through, and the Risale-i Nur helps with that progress.

questions.question: Why does the speaker mention an imagined question-and-answer talk?
questions.answer: To share a short form of an important discussion about the purpose of the Risale-i Nur.

questions.question: What does the passage say a tiny portion of the Risale-i Nur can already do?
questions.answer: It can overcome the arguments of very stubborn deniers.

questions.question: What is the first side of the conversation impressed by?
questions.answer: It is impressed by how strong the Risale-i Nur is in defending belief.

questions.question: What image helps explain the size of the religious damage?
questions.answer: The passage uses the picture of a giant stronghold suffering major harm.

questions.question: What two levels of healing are contrasted in the passage?
questions.answer: It contrasts healing one person’s inner self with healing the wider community’s shared spiritual state.

questions.question: How have harmful forces been described in the passage?
questions.answer: They are described as carefully prepared tools of corruption built up over a very long time.

questions.question: Why does the passage speak about many medicines instead of just one?
questions.answer: Because the sickness is described as large and complicated, so many kinds of healing are needed.

questions.question: What kinds of solutions are said to be needed?
questions.answer: Very certain proofs, strong supports, and highly effective spiritual remedies are needed.

questions.question: What two big jobs of the Risale-i Nur are mentioned near the end?
questions.answer: It heals major damage to faith and helps believers advance in faith.

questions.question: What is the title topic of this passage?
questions.answer: It is about the purpose of the Risale-i Nur.

questions.question: What does the phrase about complete readiness suggest about the Risale-i Nur?
questions.answer: It suggests serious effort, careful preparation, and full dedication.

questions.question: What does the passage say the Risale-i Nur is not limited to fixing?
questions.answer: It is not limited to fixing a small problem or helping only one person’s inner feelings.

questions.question: What larger duty is it said to be doing instead?
questions.answer: It is repairing very great harm affecting Islam in a wide and serious way.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the scale of this work compared with a small house?
questions.answer: It says the work is far greater, like restoring an enormous stronghold.

questions.question: Why are very strong proofs needed?
questions.answer: They are needed because the wounds are huge and widespread, so weak answers would not be enough.
